_comment: Field journal birds: real Perth species. hours: [[from, to], ...] in game hours (to < from wraps past midnight). perch: ground, tree, water, shore, post or air. habitats: habitat tags (data/field/habitats.json) unless places names zones outright. rarity 1 common .. 4 very rare. value: AUD for a two-star print. shy 0..1 makes the shot harder. source traffic: the bird comes from traffic's wildlife (not spawned here). Looks: model is the body plan (scripts/field/bird_models.gd PLANS); colours body, wing, head, belly, beak, plus optional breast, tail, legs, eye, neck, foreneck, crest, lower, pouch, underwing, undertail; marks [[kind, colour]] are painted patches, later ones on top (head: cap, crown, forehead, nape, face, cheek, ear, mask, sub_mask, brow, lores, throat, tear, whisker, eye_ring, eye_patch, spectacles, face_disc; neck: hindneck, collar, foreneck, neck_low, neck_stripe; body: breast, breast_band, bib, mantle, rump, vent, flanks, belly_patch and patterns bars_under, spots_under, streaks_under, scallops, mottle; wings: shoulder, wing_panel, wingbar(s), wing_edge, tertials, speculum, primaries, flight, flight_feathers, carpal, wing_spots; tail: tail_tip, tail_band, tail_edge, tail_corners, tail_panel, tail_bars; bill: bill_tip, bill_band, bill_base; shield, wattle and lobe are shapes); shape scales parts (neck, bill, tail, crest, head, body, leg, wing, eye, reach) or sets a plan value (tilt, droop, hook, tail_kind, wing_kind, hackles). Wrong birds (wrong: true) come after midnight once Discoveries has `after`; spot is a place (habitat or photo spot id, or home_pole, shed_roof, barrack_crossing); behaviour: watch, sing, still, silent, lights, nest, house; page is M.'s 1979 journal page (page_by: you for the last).

birds.name: Australian magpie
birds.hint: Any lawn in daylight.
birds.note: Carols at first light and defends its patch in spring. Every Perth park has a family.

birds.name: Australian white ibis
birds.hint: Russell Square, Hyde Park, the foreshore.
birds.note: The bin chicken. Probes lawns with that long curved bill and roosts in the park's paperbarks.

birds.name: Rainbow lorikeet
birds.hint: Noisy in the street trees, city and parks.
birds.note: Not from here: escaped birds in the 1960s, now everywhere. Screeches in fast flocks at dusk.

birds.name: Laughing dove
birds.hint: Footpaths and backyards.
birds.note: A soft bubbling coo. Brought to Perth Zoo in 1898 and never left.

birds.name: Spotted dove
birds.hint: Gardens and verges, in pairs.
birds.note: The black collar has white spots, like a string of pearls.

birds.name: Feral pigeon
birds.hint: Stations, the Cultural Centre, under bridges.
birds.note: Nobody's favourite, but the neck shimmers green and purple in the right light.

birds.name: Willie wagtail
birds.hint: Lawns by water. Sings on moonlit nights too.
birds.note: Never still: the tail swings side to side as it hunts. Sings 'sweet pretty creature', even at night.

birds.name: Red wattlebird
birds.hint: Flowering gums and grevilleas.
birds.note: Loud, bossy and coughing. The red wattles hang from its cheeks.

birds.name: New Holland honeyeater
birds.hint: Banksia in Kings Park and Bold Park.
birds.note: Black and white streaks with yellow wing flashes and a white eye. Banksia flowers are its pub.

birds.name: Singing honeyeater
birds.hint: Coastal scrub behind the beaches.
birds.note: Drab olive with a black stripe through the eye and a rolling, cheerful song.

birds.name: Galah
birds.hint: Ovals and parks, grazing in pairs.
birds.note: Pink and grey and a bit daft. Hangs upside down from power lines for fun.

birds.name: Little corella
birds.hint: Big shrieking flocks at Hyde Park and Lake Monger, mornings and evenings.
birds.note: Not native to Perth, and loud about it. A pink smudge between the eye and the bill.

birds.name: Australian ringneck
birds.hint: Kings Park and Bold Park gums.
birds.note: Locally the 'twenty-eight', after its call. A yellow collar on a black head.

birds.name: Carnaby's black cockatoo
birds.hint: Kings Park pines and banksia, coming in to roost at dusk.
birds.note: Endangered, and only in the south-west. Their slow, wailing flocks are rain-bringers, people say.

birds.name: Laughing kookaburra
birds.hint: Kings Park and Hyde Park at dawn and dusk.
birds.note: An eastern bird brought over in the 1890s. The dawn laugh is the whole family joining in.

birds.name: Black swan
birds.hint: The river and Lake Monger.
birds.note: The state's bird, and the river is named for it. White flight feathers only show when it flies.

birds.name: Australian pelican
birds.hint: Claisebrook Cove, Point Fraser, Point Walter.
birds.note: Glides in low and lands like a jumbo. Waits by the boat ramps for fish frames.

birds.name: Pacific black duck
birds.hint: Any lake or quiet stretch of river.
birds.note: Brown with a striped face and a green flash on the wing.

birds.name: Australasian swamphen
birds.hint: Reedy lake edges: Lake Monger, Herdsman.
birds.note: Great red feet, a red shield on the face, and a habit of flicking its white undertail.

birds.name: Eurasian coot
birds.hint: Rafts of them on the lakes.
birds.note: Sooty black with a white bill and shield. Runs across the water to take off.

birds.name: Little pied cormorant
birds.hint: Posts and jetty pylons over the water.
birds.note: Dives for gobies and shrimp, then sits on a post with its wings out to dry.

birds.name: Australasian darter
birds.hint: Swims with only its snake neck out of the water.
birds.note: Spears fish with that dagger bill, then hangs its wings out like washing.

birds.name: Silver gull
birds.hint: Wherever there are chips.
birds.note: Red bill, red legs, no shame.

birds.name: Greater crested tern
birds.hint: Groynes and harbour walls, Cottesloe to Freo.
birds.note: A shaggy black crest and a yellow bill. Plunges headfirst for whitebait.

birds.name: Pied oystercatcher
birds.hint: Quiet beaches early, before the dog walkers.
birds.note: Black and white with a long carrot bill, working the wet sand in pairs.

birds.name: Eastern osprey
birds.hint: Circling over the wider river, Point Walter and Alfred Cove.
birds.note: Hovers, then drops feet first into the water. Nests on the light towers and channel markers.

birds.name: Nankeen kestrel
birds.hint: Hovering over rough grass and dunes.
birds.note: Hangs dead still in the wind, tail fanned, then drops on a grasshopper.

birds.name: White-faced heron
birds.hint: Wading the shallows, alone.
birds.note: Blue-grey with a white face, stepping slowly through the shallows.

birds.name: Great egret
birds.hint: Tall and white in the lake shallows.
birds.note: Stands perfectly still for minutes, then the neck uncoils like a spring.

birds.name: Nankeen night heron
birds.hint: Lake edges after dark. A croak overhead.
birds.note: Roosts hidden in the day and fishes at night. Cinnamon back, black cap.

birds.name: Tawny frogmouth
birds.hint: Night. On a low branch, pretending to be one.
birds.note: Not an owl. Sits stiff and points its face up so it looks like a broken branch.

birds.name: Southern boobook
birds.hint: Kings Park and Bold Park at night. Listen for 'mopoke'.
birds.note: Australia's smallest common owl, and the one saying 'boo-book' in the dark.

birds.name: Eastern barn owl
birds.hint: A pale shape over rough grass at Herdsman, deep at night.
birds.note: Heart-shaped white face. Hunts by sound alone and screeches rather than hoots.

birds.name: Rainbow bee-eater
birds.hint: Arrives for the warm months. Hawking bees over sandy ground.
birds.note: Spring migrant from the north. Nests in tunnels in sandy banks, even on golf courses.

birds.name: Splendid fairywren
birds.hint: Hopping in the low scrub of Kings Park bushland, morning.
birds.note: The breeding male is blue all over, a ridiculous blue. The family hops about with him.

birds.name: Australian raven
birds.hint: Everywhere, watching.
birds.note: White eyes and shaggy throat hackles. The long, falling 'aaah' is the sound of a hot Perth afternoon.

birds.name: Welcome swallow
birds.hint: Skimming low over water and ovals.
birds.note: Nests under bridges and jetties. Rust throat, forked tail, never lands for long.

birds.name: Grey butcherbird
birds.hint: Kings Park, on a dead branch.
birds.note: Hooked bill, beautiful piping song, and it wedges prey into forks of branches.

birds.name: Musk duck
birds.hint: Herdsman Lake, low in the water.
birds.note: The male has a leathery lobe under the bill and splashes the water with his feet to show off.

birds.name: Australian reed warbler
birds.hint: You hear it long before you see it. Thick reeds at a quiet lake edge, early or late.
birds.note: Plain brown, a pale eyebrow, and a song like someone winding a rusty clock. All spring it shouts from the reedbeds and never shows itself.

birds.name: Buff-banded rail
birds.hint: Out of the reeds for a moment at first light, then gone again. Quiet edges with mud.
birds.note: A barred, chestnut-browed rail that steps out of cover, flicks its tail, and walks straight back in. A good one to get.

birds.name: Black-winged stilt
birds.hint: Shallow mud and flats, in little groups. The legs give it away.
birds.note: Black and white, on absurd pink legs. Yaps like a small dog when you get too close.

birds.name: Frogmouth on the lane pole
birds.hint: The pole outside 15 Little Shenton Lane, after midnight.
birds.note: It turns its head to follow the car. All the way round.
birds.page: 12 February 1979. The frogmouth is on the pole outside number 15 again. It doesn't pretend to be a branch for me any more. When I pull in, its head comes round with the car, all the way round. I've started saying goodnight to it.

birds.name: Magpie singing at 2 am
birds.hint: Russell Square, in the small hours. Turn the engine off and listen.
birds.note: Not the dawn carol. It sings the tune from the station between the others, note for note.
birds.page: Russell Square, ten past two. A magpie singing in the dark, and not the morning carol. It's the tune from the station, the one between the others, note for note. I sat in the car until it stopped. It stopped when I turned the radio off.

birds.name: Swan facing upstream
birds.hint: Off Riverside Drive, where the lights come up off the water.
birds.note: Dead still in the current, facing upstream. It doesn't drift.
birds.page: Riverside Drive, 3 am. One swan, dead still in the current, facing upstream like it's waiting for someone. The river lights came up around it and it didn't move. I counted to six hundred. It didn't drift an inch.

birds.name: Thirteen black cockatoos
birds.hint: The gums on Fraser Avenue at 3 am. Count them.
birds.note: Thirteen, silent, in the gums at 3 am. Always thirteen.
birds.page: Fraser Avenue, 3 am. Thirteen black cockatoos in the lemon gums. Cockatoos don't sit up at night and they don't sit quiet. I came back three nights running and it was thirteen every time. I've stopped counting. They haven't.

birds.name: Ibis in the Barrack Street crossing
birds.hint: Barrack Street and the Terrace, late. In the middle of the road.
birds.note: It stands on the white line. When it lifts its head, the lights change.
birds.page: Barrack Street and the Terrace, twenty to two. An ibis standing on the white line, where the cars would be if there were any. Every time it lifted its head the lights changed. I watched for an hour to be sure. I'm sure.

birds.name: Boobook with tape in its nest
birds.hint: The bush side of Kings Park, in the small hours. Look for something shining in a nest.
birds.note: Its nest is woven through with brown cassette tape.
birds.page: Kings Park, the bush side, 2 am. A boobook by a hollow in a marri, and the nest is lined with brown ribbon. It's cassette tape. A bit of label was caught on a twig: NIGHT DR. I haven't made that one yet.

birds.name: A small grey bird
birds.hint: On the shed roof.
birds.note: Small, grey, no markings at all. It isn't in any field guide.
birds.page: Shed roof, 15 Little Shenton Lane. Small and grey, no markings at all. It doesn't look at the car. It looks at the house. It isn't in any of the books. I think it's been here the whole time.
